accepted.question_text: For the antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg XXX spin chain, consider ground-state correlation functions of local spin operators on sequential lattice sites, including quantities such as the emptiness formation probability. These correlation functions are known to be expressible as polynomials in ln 2 and in values of the Riemann zeta function, or equivalently the alternating zeta series, at odd arguments with rational coefficients. Find an efficient and tractable description of the rational coefficients that appear in these polynomial expressions.

evidence.quote: Conjecture. 1 (Boos, Korepin 2001) Any correlation function of the XXX spin chain can be represented as a polynomial in ln 2 and values of Riemann zeta function at odd arguments with rational coefficients [13],[14].

However we still not have explicit expressions for the rational coefficients that enter in the expression for the correlation functions as polynomials in ln 2 and Riemann zeta function at odd arguments. Such a description will provide a tractable formula for the correlations of the XXX spin chain.

Open problem: Efficient description of the rational coefficients which appear in the expression for the correlation functions of the XXX spin chain as a polynomial in alternating zeta series at odd arguments.

accepted.question_text: Let A be a block of neighboring spins in the ground state of the XXZ spin chain and let ρ_A be the reduced density matrix obtained by tracing out the rest of the chain. The entanglement of the block is measured by the von Neumann entropy S(ρ_A) = -Tr(ρ_A ln ρ_A). In the gapped antiferromagnetic regime Δ < -1, determine analytically the limiting value S(∞) approached by the entropy of a large block as the number of spins in the block tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: The density matrix of the subsystem A obtained by tracing away the B degrees of freedom is ρ_A = Tr_B(ρ_{A&B}). In a seminal paper [19] Bennet, Bernstein, Popescu and Schumacher discovered that the von Neumann entropy of a subsystem A S(ρ_A) = −Tr(ρ_A ln ρ_A) is a measure of entanglement.
In the gapped antiferromagnetic case (∆ < −1) we expect that S(ρ(n)) will tend to a limiting value S(∞) but at this moment the analytic evaluation of this constant is missing.
Open problem: For the XXZ spin chain in the antiferromagnetic region (∆ < −1) calculate the limiting value of the entropy of a subsystem when the number of spins in the block is large.

accepted.question_text: For the XXZ spin chain in the critical regime -1 ≤ Δ < 1, study time- and temperature-dependent correlation functions at large separation in space and time, including the correlation function g(n,t) discussed in the paper. Derive an explicit analytic formula for the asymptotic exponential decay of these correlation functions in the joint large-distance, large-time limit.

evidence.quote: Despite these considerable efforts the asymptotics of time and temperature dependent correlation functions, such as g(n, t) (see 13) for the XXZ spin chain, are still out of our reach. We expect that they will decay exponentially like in the previous examples of the isotropic XY spin chain or the δ-function Bose gas but at this moment we do not have such a result.
Open problem: Derive an explicit analytic formula describing the asymptotic exponential decay of time and temperature correlation functions in the critical region (−1 ≤ ∆ < 1) of the XXZ spin chain.

accepted.question_text: In the six-vertex model on a square lattice with domain wall boundary conditions, the arrows on the upper and lower boundaries point into the lattice while the arrows on the left and right boundaries point out. Determine the bulk correlation functions and the boundary correlation functions for this model, despite the loss of translation invariance caused by the boundary conditions.

evidence.quote: By domain wall boundary conditions we understand the situation in which the arrows on the upper and lower boundaries point in the square lattice and the ones on the left and right boundaries point out.

As in all exactly solvable models the study of correlation functions is of extreme importance. In the case of the six vertex model with DWBC an added difficulty is constituted by the lack of translation invariance.
Open problem: Calculate the bulk and boundary correlation functions of the six vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions.

accepted.question_text: Generalize domain wall boundary conditions from the six-vertex model to other integrable models in such a way that the partition function retains the key determinant property: it should be representable as a determinant whose dimension is proportional to the size of the system.

evidence.quote: Using the recursion relations Izergin was able to derive a determinantal formula for the partition function.
The main feature of formula (19) is the fact that the partition function of the six vertex model with DWBC is expressed as a determinant of the size of the system.

Open problem: Obtain generalizations of domain wall boundary conditions for other models such that the partition function is expressed as a determinant of a dimension proportional with the size of the system.
